headline: Valve changes Steam release rules after AI game flood causes review backlog, delaying indie titles
summary: Valve's new requirements aim to clear a backlog that has extended game review times to 12 business days, impacting indie developers and their launch schedules.
details: Valve is updating its game release rules to address a significant backlog in approvals, largely due to a recent surge of new titles, many created with AI. This has caused indie games to miss launch dates, sometimes by weeks. Valve's target for new title reviews is 3-5 days, but it's currently taking up to 12 business days.

The new rules require developers to run their games through Steam for at least five minutes to ensure platform compatibility. They must also confirm common redistributables like DirectX and Visual C++, check achievement readiness, configure Steam Cloud save paths, and categorize screenshots.

The company aims to avoid re-reviews that contribute to longer wait times, acknowledging the stress developers face. This move comes as the store has been reportedly flooded by "AI vibe-coded games" with insufficient pre-release checks.

Developer 2 Left Thumbs noted a spike in review times around September/October, attributing it partly to the "overwhelming amount of slop now flooding Steam." This data is supported by Reddit user u/ploz, who found that 49.9% of games released on Steam in October disclosed AI-generated content.

In June, nearly 20% of Next Fest game demos also disclosed the use of AI. These delays have real consequences for developers, with one, structmira of Cubic Earth, reporting lost momentum and player complaints due to missed launch windows.

topic: tencent hy4 ai can see and use your computer
headline_marked: [[Tencent's Hy4 can see and use your computer]], a 770B-parameter model now available via API
headline: Tencent's Hy4 can see and use your computer, a 770B-parameter model now available via API
summary: Tencent's new 770B-parameter Hy4 model is the first in its Hunyuan line to combine visual understanding with the ability to operate a computer via GUI and command line. It's currently accessible via APIs, with open weights coming soon.
details: Tencent has released Hy4, its new-generation large language model, featuring 770 billion total parameters in a mixture-of-experts architecture. This marks a significant scale jump from its predecessor, Hy3's 295 billion parameters.

Hy4 is the first model in Tencent's Hunyuan line that can 'see' through fine-grained image processing, complex chart analysis, and mathematical visual reasoning. Crucially, it is also the first that can 'use' a computer, operating a machine via its graphical interface and command line.

The model is currently available through Tencent's own platforms like Tencent Cloud TokenHub, WorkBuddy/CodeBuddy, Yuanbao, ima, and the WeCom intelligent assistant Dayuan. It's also accessible via APIs on OpenRouter, Hermes, and OpenCode.
While Tencent frames Hy4 as an open-weight model, the weights themselves are not yet released, with a promise of open-sourcing soon. For now, users can interact with the hosted model as a service.

The mixture-of-experts architecture means only a fraction of its 770 billion parameters activates for any given token. This design allows such a large model to remain servable, and its total capacity should not be directly compared to dense model parameter counts.

Beyond its core visual and computer-use capabilities, Tencent reports stronger instruction following, improved long-document understanding, and longer-horizon agent task execution. The context window is listed at 1,048,576 tokens on OpenRouter's listing.

Tencent highlights Hy4 as the first Hunyuan model to combine visual understanding and computer use, positioning it among the strongest open-weight models available. However, Tencent also acknowledges that Hy4 trails leading closed models in research mathematics.
An independent data point from the South China Morning Post noted that the Hy4 preview achieved a 23rd-place ranking on WebDev, a global AI benchmark leaderboard.

Hy4 is significant for three reasons: it signals the frontier's direction towards models that perceive screens and act on machines, the open-weights promise matters for broader adoption, and its competitive context against other large, capable models will shape its reception.
